newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy magistrates reopen part of Fiat probe.
newsitem.headline: Italy magistrates reopen part of Fiat probe.

text.p: Italian magistrates have reopened an inquiry into accounts of companies within the Fiat group and told chairman Cesare Romiti and his finance director they may face questioning, ANSA news agency said on Saturday.

ANSA reported that magistrates in Fiat's home city of Turin had sent notice to Romiti and finance chief Francesco Paolo Mattioli and were pursuing new angles in an investigation of 1992-93 accounts at Fiat's construction companies Cogefar and Impresit.
Fiat lawyer Vittorio Chiusano said neither he nor his assistants had received any notification from Turin magistrates.

Romiti was given an 18-month suspended jail sentence by a Turin court in April for false accounting at Italy's largest private industrial giant, while Mattioli, on trial with him, received a 16-month sentence. Both men are appealing.

ANSA said the current inquiry was related to the case which culminated in the April sentences. Magistrates had decided to renew this particular line of inquiry after reconsidering an earlier decision to shelve the investigation.
